22071.notes: Orleans Parish / City of New Orleans. Effective January 1, 2026 Louisiana shifted from ownership bid-down tax sales to true tax lien certificates with interest bidding and multi-year redemption. City Treasury tax sale/adjudication pages note process changes for 2026 (details rolling out on nola.gov Treasury). Recent pre-reform cycles used CivicSource online certificate sales (e.g. Oct 2025 for multi-year delinquencies). Separate Orleans Parish Sheriff civil sales (Thursdays noon) are primarily mortgage/judgment executions, not the city tax lien auction. Prefer quality: verify live 2026 Treasury instructions before capital deployment.
22071.auctionFormat: Online (tax lien certificates; platform per City Treasury notice — historically CivicSource)

auctionPlatform.label: City of New Orleans Treasury — Tax Sales / Tax Lien Certificates (see also CivicSource)

22071.auctionFrequency: Annual city tax lien/certificate sale as advertised by Treasury (historically multi-day fall windows); confirm 2026 dates on nola.gov
22071.depositRules: Follow City Treasury and platform bidder packet for the active sale year (registration, deposits, certified funds). Pre-2026 CivicSource cycles had platform-specific rules; post-2026 lien statute changes mechanics — do not assume old ownership-sale terms still apply.

taxCollector.label: City of New Orleans Department of Finance / Treasury

clerkOfCourt.label: Orleans Parish Civil District Court Clerk / Recorder of Mortgages

22071.survivingLiens: Under the 2026 lien system, buyers acquire a certificate lien, not immediate fee title. Federal liens, code liens, and title clouds are common in Orleans — full abstract essential. Sheriff judicial sales follow different extinction rules.
22071.quietTitle: Essential in practice for marketable title after tax lien foreclosure/adjudication in New Orleans given historic notice and adjudication litigation risk.

24013.notes: Maryland tax sale certificate (lien) county. Carroll County 2026 online tax sale at carroll.marylandtaxsale.com: bidding Monday June 29, 2026 8:00 a.m. through Tuesday June 30, 2026 12:00 p.m. Online registration required (opened June 1, 2026; closed June 19, 2026 2:00 p.m. per published notice). Highest bidder receives tax sale certificate, not deed; owner may redeem; foreclosure of right of redemption is separate court process under Tax-Property Art. Title 14 Subtitle 8.

auctionPlatform.label: RealAuction — Carroll County MD Tax Sale

24013.auctionFrequency: Annual (2026: June 29–30, 2026 online); DAT statewide schedule lists Carroll late June
24013.depositRules: Online registration on carroll.marylandtaxsale.com within published window; platform ACH registration fee and bank verification per RealAuction MD county pattern. taxCollector.label: Carroll County Tax Collection / Bureau of Revenue

24013.survivingLiens: Certificate is a lien senior to many private interests but does not wipe title until successful foreclosure of redemption. Federal tax liens and some municipal charges require analysis. Certificate typically valid ~2 years before foreclosure path.
24013.quietTitle: After foreclosure of right of redemption, title insurers often still require quiet title or curative work before free-and-clear insurance.

24027.notes: Maryland tax sale certificate county. auctionPlatform.label: Howard County Finance — Property Tax Sale portal

26065.notes: Michigan tax deed / foreclosure auction county (not a lien certificate sale). After multi-year delinquency and circuit court judgment of foreclosure (typically March), title vests in County Treasurer who auctions fee-simple parcels. Ingham is one of few MI counties still using live in-person auctions (with Bippus). 2026 first auction: Wednesday August 26, 2026, 10:00 a.m., Lansing Center. Properties often blighted; open houses and code packets published. Treasurer may cancel any sale anytime under MCL 211.78m(2).

auctionPlatform.label: Ingham County Treasurer Land Sale Auction (Bippus / Lansing Center)

26065.auctionFrequency: Two auctions per year (1st ~late August; 2nd later for unsold) — 2026 first auction Aug 26, 2026 10:00 a.m.
26065.depositRules: Pre-register at BippusUSA.com; on-site registration from 8:30 a.m. Show $2,000 cash/certified funds for bidder card (applied to deposit if you win). 10% of purchase price deposit (min $2,000) by 4:30 p.m. sale day; balance within 14 days. Purchase price includes bid + 10% auctioneer fee + $30 deed recording (+ performance bond if demo order). Cash/certified funds/cashier’s checks only. Delinquent taxpayers and red-tagged owners barred.

clerkOfCourt.label: Ingham County Register of Deeds / Circuit Court Clerk

propertyAppraiser.label: Ingham County Equalization / local assessors (BS&A online)

26065.survivingLiens: Judgment of foreclosure generally extinguishes most junior private liens, but federal tax liens, certain easements, and post-foreclosure issues need review. Buyer takes as-is condition/code violations. Surplus proceeds claims process exists for former owners under Michigan law post-Rafaeli.
26065.quietTitle: Often still used for marketable title insurance comfort even after tax deed, especially with code or notice issues.
